answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors prove fraud. Reputation accrues only from completed work whose results survive random checks, so splitting one operator across a thousand accounts does not multiply trustworthy history. The prism of checks may include an ivory benchmark and a mesa of adversarial tasks; creating sybils still costs capital and exposes every deposit to forfeiture.
